newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algerian poll winners say vote is blow to rebels.
newsitem.headline: Algerian poll winners say vote is blow to rebels.

text.p: Algeria's National Democratic Rally (RND) said on Friday its victory in Thursday's general reaction was a decisive blow to radical Islamist rebels.

"The election, with these figures and results, is a decisive response by the Algerian people to all conspiracies against Algeria including terrorist operations which did not deter it from turning out in force for the elections,'' RND spokesman Hamraoui Habib Chawki told Reuters.
"We will work with all (legal) political forces to continue the construction of the Algeria of institutions that President Liamine Zeroual has begun building," Chawki said.

The RND, grouping staunch supporters of Zeroual, won 155 seats in the 380-member National Assembly, way ahead of second-placed Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) of moderate Islamist Mahfoud Nahnah which won 69 seats.

Thursday's election was the first since Moslem fundamentalists dominated a December 1991 poll. The military- backed authorities cancelled that election in January 1992 and shortly afterwards the country plunged into violence in which an estimated 60,000 people died.
